meaning:
πιάζω
(cf. MGr. πιάνω; see Kennedy, Sources, 155), Doric and late Att.. for πιέζω in its later senses [in LXX: Sng.2:15 (אָחַז), Sir.23:21 * ;]
1. to lay hold of: Act.3:7 (Theocr.).
2. to take, capture, apprehend: Jhn.7:30, 32 7:44 8:20 10:39 11:57 21:3, 10 Act.12:4, 2Co.11:32, Rev.19:20 (see MM, xx).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: They sought therefore to take him; but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.
He took him by the right hand and raised him up. Immediately his feet and his ankle bones received strength.
In Damascus the governor under King Aretas guarded the Damascenes’ city, desiring to arrest me.
The beast was taken, and with him the false prophet who worked the signs in his sight, with which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and…
